title: Tin whistle
reference_instrument: a different whistle, for its held sound only and with no count: a Sweetone D tin whistle playing a slurred D major scale, cut between the slurs (Mirjam Plas, Escola Superior de Musica de Catalunya, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0). It is not the modelled Clare whistle, and no note of it stands alone
summary: Nothing here is graded: no licensed whistle recording is in the library, and the clip beside each note is a different whistle's slurred scale. Every note sounds flat of its name, 10 to 46 c on the scale, from a pull the model doesn't explain, and its harmonics don't follow the real one's. This is a Clare D whistle built from the ISVR measurements of one real whistle (Davies, Pinho and English 2006): bore, six finger holes, flue, window and pocket, blown at each note's printed air flow through a forced Bickley jet. It carries Fletcher's 1976 jet spreading as a trial, breath noise, and a labium offset borrowed from the recorder. D6 alone also has the jet swing limit. It models the paper's metered-air rig, not a player: no tonguing, breath or finger motion.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a forced Bickley jet driven by a mouth pressure computed from each note's printed air flow through the card's windway law, with the 1.48 mm flue, acting on a connected duct network
The bore and six finger holes from the same paper, open or closed per its fingering chart, with the open holes' inner radiation matched in series, and the closed pocket behind the flue
The window's acoustic mass from its own 3-D wall cut, and its radiation from the outer face of the head's cylinder
The contraction loss at the flue exit (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I, vena-contracta coefficient 0.6)
Jet spreading by Fletcher 1976, a trial here: this flue is outside its measured 0.25 to 1.0 mm
A labium offset of 0.203 mm, 0.1374 flue heights, borrowed from the recorder (Bouterse 2010), because we have no printed whistle value. It gives the even harmonics a level at all
Breath noise at the window edge (Verge 1995): gain 1.3e-3 of the jet's dynamic pressure, opening at a flue Reynolds number of 700 (p. 196), through an order-two Butterworth band-pass

On D6 only, a limit on how far the jet can swing: Fletcher 1976's envelope, applied in time our own way. It lets the first harmonic lead on that note. On D5, G5 and B5 it makes the match worse, so it stays off
Dry air at 20 C, because the paper blew the whistle from a metered supply, and Stokes-Kirchhoff air along the path to the receiver
A physical receiver 1 m above the window, summing every open aperture, with the compact radiation load declared valid to 2.8 kHz
physics_missing: A graded comparison: the clip beside each note is a Sweetone D whistle's slurred scale, cut between the slurs, so only its held sound compares, with no count. A second whistle's scale differs from it by 3 to 17 dB on single harmonics, so one recording doesn't fix a target closer than that

Pitch: on the scale the notes read D5 -16, E5 -35, F#5 -46, G5 -35, A5 -41, B5 -31, C#6 -36 and D6 -10 c. A scratch model with no jet puts the passive modes of D5, G5, B5 and D6 18 to 48 c above where the renders sound with wall loss on, so the jet pulls the notes flat. No pressure was chosen to correct it

The real whistle's spectrum: on D5, G5 and B5, H2 is 32 to 35 dB under H1, against 17 to 25 on this whistle, and H5 stands 14 to 33 dB over it. On D6, H3 is -3.7 dB re H1 against -27, and H2 stands well over this whistle's

A jet drive from print that works here. Refused on these notes: the Auvray 2014 jet drive (wrong note on 10 of 11 whistle notes), the Ernoult-Fabre window mass, the unsteady windway with the forced jet, and the de la Cuadra 2005 exit law, whose Reynolds range excludes this flue. The momentum drive of Thwaites and Fletcher 1983 silences B5 and D6 and moves G5 to its third mode
A player: no tonguing, breath or finger motion. The bore holds dry air, as in the paper's rig, not breath
Attack and release: only the held sound can be compared. In the scale each note's output reaches digital silence 0.13 to 0.19 s after its release starts, so nothing rings beyond that
Overblown notes: none are posted. Only the paper's measured operating points were rendered, so where each register begins and any hysteresis are unmapped
Pages for E5, F#5, A5 and C#6: they appear only in the scale and melody, on cards with the same edits as the posted four, without the swing limit

The flue's true taper, the pocket's shape, the thin hole wall, hole shape and undercut, and the bore's narrowing at the wedge. Where the wedge tip sits in the wall isn't published, and the cards use one end of that bracket
A measured jet card: these cards use the repository's interim one
